procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism through the Factory Registration service, which requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added; registration takes about three working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Fill in the application form with the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product.
Upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online: AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.
Submit the application and wait for approval, or a return with comments to correct; processing takes about one working day.

The certificate is valid for twelve months from the date of issue, covers only one import, and must be issued before, at or within five working days of export; it can be issued retrospectively up to twelve months from shipment with 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed.
Keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The tariff schedule prints 15%, but an exemption notification lowers the duty actually charged to 10%; the effective rate is used.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources.
